grh_63eed254d325aad1fd00.title: The Sea Wolf
paragraphs: After a ferry disaster, writer Humphrey Van Weyden and a young woman named Ruth are rescued by the sealing schooner Ghost, commanded by the brutal and intellectually formidable Wolf Larsen. Larsen rules his crew through fear, mocks compassion and religion, and refuses to let his unwilling passengers leave, forcing Van Weyden to confront a philosophy built entirely on strength and survival. As the voyage worsens, Larsen begins suffering violent headaches and periods of blindness, while his abused crew grows mutinous. An attack by Larsenâ€™s brother leaves the Ghost sinking and the crew gone. Van Weyden gets Ruth away in a lifeboat, then returns for supplies and finds Larsen alone, blind, and waist-deep in rising water. Larsen tries to keep Van Weyden with him so he will not die alone, but cannot stop his escape. The sinking captain is left reciting scripture, finally receiving the one thing he had never asked of anyone before: company at the edge of death.

grh_6364bd531b2538c4b535.title: Broken Arrow
paragraphs: Prospector Tom Jeffords comes to believe peace is possible between white settlers and the Chiricahua Apache and earns the trust of Cochise. Jeffords helps bring General Howard to negotiate a three-month armistice and later a treaty based on Apache equality and security on their own land. During the peace effort Jeffords marries Apache woman Sonseeahray, but renegade whites led by Slade ambush them and kill her. Grief-stricken Jeffords wants revenge, yet Cochise refuses to let either bad whites or bad Indians destroy the agreement. The armistice holds, and Sonseeahray's death becomes part of the sacrifice that seals a lasting peace.
